How do you fix a flat bike tire?

You'll need tire levers, a new tube (or patch kit), and a pump. Here's the drill:

  2. Deflate fully, then use levers to pry one bead off the rim.

  5. Install the new tube (or patch), tuck the bead back on by hand.
  6. Inflate slowly to seat the bead, then pump to recommended pressure.
  7. Reinstall wheel, reconnect brake, and test ride.

Pro tip: line up the tire label with the valve stem so you can find punctures faster next time.

You're on the shoulder with a flat. What's the safe order for swapping on the spare?

Pull off the road, hazards on. Then:

  1. Park on flat ground, set the parking brake. If you have a manual, leave it in gear; auto, shift to Park.
  2. Loosen the lug nuts a quarter turn while the tire is still on the ground. If they won't budge, stand on the wrench—carefully.
  3. Place the jack under the car's designated lift point (check the manual; usually a notch or arrow on the rocker panel). Raise until the flat tire is just off the ground.
  4. Remove the lug nuts and pull the tire straight off. It may need a firm tug.
  5. Lift the spare on, line up the holes, and hand-tighten the lug nuts in a star pattern. Snug them, don't crank yet.
  6. Lower the car until the tire touches the ground, then tighten the nuts firmly in a star pattern.

Spare tires are often temporary: keep under 50 mph and get the real tire fixed or replaced soon. Re-torque the lug nuts after about 50 miles.

The toilet runs and runs. What's the usual culprit and the cheap fix?

Most likely: the flapper (rubber seal at the tank bottom) isn't sealing, so water leaks into the bowl and the fill valve keeps topping up.

  1. Turn off the water at the shut-off valve behind the toilet. Flush to empty the tank.
  2. Lift the tank lid and set it somewhere safe.
  3. Check the flapper: if it's warped, cracked, or covered in slime, replace it. A new flapper costs a couple of dollars.
  4. Also check the chain: too tight holds the flapper open; too loose lets it slip under. Adjust for a little slack.
  5. If the water level is above the overflow tube, adjust the fill valve float so the tank stops filling about an inch below the top of the tube.

Turn the water back on and watch. If it still runs, the fill valve itself may need replacing—also inexpensive and usually a screw-on job.

The screw head is stripped and won't turn. What now?

Try these in order, easiest first:

  1. Rubber band trick: Place a wide rubber band over the screw head, press the screwdriver into it, and turn slowly. The rubber fills the gaps and adds grip.
  2. Bigger screwdriver: If the head is Phillips, try the next size up. Sometimes the original was too small and rounded the edges.
  3. Pliers: If the head sticks out, grab it with locking pliers and turn.
  4. Screw extractor: A dedicated bit (sold in kits) bites into the stripped head and backs it out. You'll need a drill to use it.
  5. Cut a new slot: With a rotary tool or hacksaw, cut a slot across the head and use a flathead screwdriver.

If the screw is in wood and you've tried everything, you may need to drill out the head and use a plug cutter or a larger screw nearby. Last resort.

Cut cells release a sulfur compound. It wafts up, hits the water film on your eyes, and turns into a mild acid. Tearing up is your eyes rinsing themselves. Nothing personal.

Inside the closing quote mark, always. "I'll be there," she said. In US style, commas and periods live inside the quotation marks even when they logically belong to the outer sentence.

If the words after the quote are a tag (said, asked, whispered), use a comma and keep the tag lowercase:

What do the numbers on a tire sidewall mean?

Take the code 205/55 R16 91V. Each part tells you something:

  • 205 — width in millimetres.

  • R — radial construction (most cars).

  • V — speed rating. V ≈ 240 km/h (149 mph).

If you fall down in a crowd, what’s the safest position?

Roll into a fetal position, cover your head with your arms, and try to get up as soon as possible. Shout for help.

Performing CPR
What are the steps for adult CPR?

1. Check responsiveness and breathing. 2. Call emergency services. 3. Place heel of hand on center of chest, other hand on top. 4. Push hard and fast at least 2 inches deep, 100–120 compressions per minute. 5. Continue until help arrives.

How deep should compressions be for an adult?

At least 2 inches (5 cm), but not more than 2.4 inches (6 cm). Allow full recoil between compressions.

What should you do first when using an AED?

Can you touch the person during defibrillation?

No. Ensure no one is touching the person when the shock is delivered. Then immediately resume CPR.

What to Do in a House Fire
If you wake up to a fire, what’s the first thing to do?

Get out immediately. Stay low to avoid smoke, check doors with the back of your hand before opening, and once out, stay out.

How can you prepare for a house fire?

Install smoke alarms on every level, test monthly, practice an escape plan twice a year, and designate a meeting spot outside.

Treating a Burn
What should you do immediately for a minor burn?

Cool the burn under cool (not cold) running water for 10–20 minutes. Remove rings or tight items before swelling. Cover loosely with sterile gauze.

What should you avoid putting on a burn?

Don’t use ice, butter, ointments, or fluffy cotton. These can worsen the injury or cause infection.
